heading: Ruby waits for a real Yon endpoint
summary: A Ruby HTTPClient is a class whose methods have empty bodies, such as `def read` with `end` on the next line. Tachyon writes each method. The `# @return [Greeting]` comment above the method names the answer: Tachyon reads the answer into the model `Greeting` from `client/models`. `# @return [Array<Greeting>]` reads a list of models, and `String`, `Integer`, `Float` or `Boolean` read a plain value. `Hash` and `Object` keep the answer as it is. An answer of another shape raises a `BehaviorError` whose `behavior_code` is `HTTP_RESPONSE`, and a failed request raises the code of the browser transport, such as `HTTP_STATUS`. A service gets the client with `#[Needs]` above `attr_reader :greeting_client`, with `# @return [GreetingClient]` between them, and calls it from an ordinary method. Ruby has no async keyword, so Tachyon runs each call of a service method in its own Ruby fiber. When the method does not wait, the page gets its answer at once. When it waits for the server, the fiber pauses, the page keeps working, other calls to the service run, and the page gets a promise that settles when the method returns. `OnStart` cannot wait: a request there fails with `HTTP_REQUEST`. `GreetingSetup` adds no adapter, so the request goes to the server of the page: the same origin, without cookies. `Cached` lets the browser cache answer a read, and after a successful `ClearCache` the next read asks the server again; a failed `ClearCache` keeps the cached answer. `OverrideSetup` gives `OverrideClient` its own adapter, and that adapter answers instead of the network. Removing the component cancels the request, and the promise is rejected with the code `CANCELLED`. A Ruby test unit runs in CRuby and has no browser transport: there a client without an adapter fails with `Required behavior adapter is missing.` The server half of this example is a plain JavaScript controller. A controller in TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Groovy, C#, F#, Kotlin, Rust, Go, Dart, Ruby, Lua or C++ answers in the same way (see Controllers), so this section shows only the browser side in other languages.
